thread:
sam: Heads up — linux alloc shard CI is red on main after the PR merge. Failing test: alloc_shard_integration (multiple flakes). Job: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/2345. Can someone help kick off a bisect? I think last-green was f3b2c9a5 (short).

ci-bot: CI Job 2345 failed · Step: alloc-test.sh · exit 1. Logs uploaded: https://ci.redwood.com/jobs/2345/logs · Rerun available via the UI.

elaine: I can repro locally: `./bazel test //alloc:shard_integration` fails for me too. Log shows `ASSERT failed: free_list corrupted` in allocator/compact.cc around line 412.

ravi: I can run a git bisect on infra machines tomorrow morning. Sam — can you paste the full last-good commit hash?

sam: Full good: f3b2c9a5d4b1e0c9a77f2b1e5c3d9a0b1c2d3e4f. First bad seems to coincide with PR #4321 (author @alex) but could be a transitive dep bump. @alex did you touch allocator internals?

alex: I only changed a small perf path in allocator/compact.cc and some comments in #4321, nothing that should touch free lists. I’ll double-check my changes.

maria: :eyes: I can run the bisect script on the infra runner. Quick checklist: try `bazel test //alloc:shard_integration --runs_per_test=1 --test_output=errors` first to get deterministic failure logs, then run bisect.

ravi: Starting bisect now from an infra worker: 
```
git bisect start
git bisect bad HEAD
git bisect good f3b2c9a5d4b1e0c9
# using CI runner to build/test each step:
./tools/ci/bisect-runner.sh --test //alloc:shard_integration
```
Will post updates as CI completes each step.

ci-bot: Bisect job queued: https://ci.redwood.com/bisect/789 · tracking in that job. It will post the first-bad commit here when finished.

tim: If bisect points to allocator core, recommend revert of the offending PR asap and open hotfix. If it's a deps bump, we may need to pin back. Tagging @eng-oncall for visibility.

ci-bot: Bisect complete — first-bad commit: a9d1e7b6c3e4f8b2a5d6e7f8. Commit author: @julien; PR 4338 touched third_party/fastalloc and bumped to v2.3. Link: https://ci.redwood.com/bisect/789/result · suspect: third_party change.

elaine: Confirmed I can reproduce with commit a9d1e7b6 locally. The failure happens after the fastalloc bump; memory layout appears different and triggers free-list invariant. I'll open a hotfix PR to pin fastalloc back.

alex: Thanks for finding that. Good catch — PR 4321 was red herring then. @sam please queue revert/pin and we can roll a hotfix release. :thumbsup:

sam: Will queue a revert of the fastalloc bump and cut a hotfix. I'll also add a quick postmortem doc in #postmortems once deploy is green. Thanks everyone for the quick responses.
